stem: A company sends traffic from its data center to a VPC over a private line: an AWS Direct Connect connection with a transit virtual interface that reaches the VPC through a Direct Connect gateway and a transit gateway. Dozens of applications send data over this connection. A new security rule says that all traffic on this connection must be encrypted in transit. The connection is a 1 Gbps hosted connection from a Direct Connect Partner. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Turn on MACsec for the Direct Connect connection, and configure the matching MACsec keys on the company router at the Direct Connect location.
options.why: MACsec is [not supported on 1 Gbps dedicated connections](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-macsec-not-on-1gbps-or-hosted) or on [any hosted connections](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-macsec-not-on-1gbps-or-hosted), so it cannot run on this connection.
options.misconception: MACsec works on every Direct Connect connection, hosted ones included

options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN on the transit gateway that runs IPsec over the Direct Connect connection, and route VPC traffic through its tunnels.
options.why: A private IP VPN can [deploy IPsec VPN over Direct Connect](../facts/site-to-site-vpn.md#site-to-site-vpn-private-ip-vpn-ipsec-over-dx-no-public-ip) on the existing transit virtual interface, so one network change encrypts all the traffic without changes in the applications.

options.text: Keep the current design, because traffic on a Direct Connect connection stays off the internet and is encrypted on the private line.
options.why: Direct Connect [does not encrypt your traffic](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption) in transit by default, so the private line alone breaks the new security rule.

options.text: Turn on TLS encryption in every application that sends data between the data center and the VPC, and keep the virtual interface unchanged.
options.why: It works, because you can [use the transit encryption options for that service](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption), but changing dozens of applications is more work than one VPN.

explanation: The deciding phrase is the 1 Gbps hosted connection. Direct Connect [does not encrypt your traffic](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption) by default, so you [establish a VPN over Direct Connect](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-encrypt-private-connection-vpn-over-dx-or-macsec) or use MACsec. MACsec does not run on [any hosted connections](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-macsec-not-on-1gbps-or-hosted), which leaves the IPsec VPN. A transit virtual interface works on a [dedicated or hosted connection of any speed](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-vif-transit-access-transit-gateways-any-speed), so the VPN uses the existing one.
takeaway: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted; on a hosted connection, add an IPsec VPN instead of MACsec.
twin: If the stem said "The connection is a 10 Gbps dedicated connection, the router and location support MACsec, and the encryption must not reduce the MTU" instead: MACsec, because [MACsec does not have the same MTU](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-vpn-over-dx-adds-encryption-reduces-mtu) considerations.
say: Direct Connect isn't encrypted by default, and MACsec doesn't run on hosted connections, so I'd run an IPsec VPN over it.
